question: Why does S1 flat (0.3344) differ from B0 (0.3543, ChromaDB-era retrieval_candidates_valid.jsonl)?
sample: every 50th valid query (1,200 queries), same fine-tuned model
recent_0.3543_rerun: 2026-10-23 session 16399dbd: `evaluate_recall.py SPLIT=valid` re-scored the 2026-03-22 ChromaDB-era candidate file; no new retrieval was run.

ruled_out.fp16: fp32 re-encoding (local MPS) of 150 B0-hit/S1-miss pairs gives gt scores 0.13 below B0 (median), same as fp16
ruled_out.HNSW_vs_flat: approximate search cannot raise recall over exact search on the same vectors
ruled_out.truncation_512: gt items >512 tokens: B0 0.586 vs S1 0.590 (no gap)
ruled_out.model_or_query_encoding: 89% of pairs where both hit reproduce B0 scores within 0.01 using the current text

conclusion: The 0.020 gap comes from item text, not search method or precision. B0 scored ground-truth items much higher only where the current item has no review keywords; adding the items valid/test-period review keywords reproduces B0 scores on median, train-only keywords do not. Most likely the ChromaDB index was built from an earlier items file whose review keywords included valid/test-period reviews, so 0.3543 is likely inflated by leakage. Not proven exactly: keyword order/format of the old file cannot be reproduced.
